::: {.solutions}

**Show all your reasoning.** Total: **40 marks** · Suggested time: **55 minutes**.

Two lines settle every question below:

$$\textbf{“}A \textbf{ sufficient for } B \textbf{”} = A \Rightarrow B \qquad\qquad
\textbf{“}A \textbf{ necessary for } B \textbf{”} = B \Rightarrow A$$

When the wording is reversed (*"a necessary condition for $Q$ is $P$"*), find the **target** — it follows
the word *for* — and the **condition**, then apply the rule.

::: {.callout-important}
## The routine, and what earns the marks

For every question: **write down the exact set of cases that makes each statement true**, then compare by
inclusion.

$$P\subseteq Q\ \Rightarrow\ P\text{ sufficient}\qquad Q\subseteq P\ \Rightarrow\ P\text{ necessary}
\qquad P=Q\ \Rightarrow\ \text{both}$$

A verdict on its own scores almost nothing. **"Not sufficient" needs a counterexample** and **"sufficient"
needs an argument** — and questions asking for both directions want *two* separate pieces of work.
:::

| Section | What it covers | Marks |
|---|---|---|
| **A — Fluency** | three phrasings of one arrow, including reversed wording | 4 |
| **B — Exam standard** | six real TMUA Paper 2 questions, justified in full | 20 |
| **C — Stretch** | parameter problems and a multi-statement comparison | 16 |

# Section A — Fluency

## Question 1 **[4]**

::: {.question}
$P$ and $Q$ are statements. Write each of the following as an implication, using $\Rightarrow$.

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) $P$ **only if** $Q$. **[1]**
&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) A **sufficient** condition for $Q$ is $P$. **[1]**
&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) $Q$ is **necessary** for $P$. **[1]**
&nbsp;&nbsp;(d) All three of (a)–(c) are the same statement. Say in one sentence how you can tell, and
name the one phrase among them whose wording points the other way. **[1]**
:::

## Question 5 **[4]** &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">2023 · P2 Q7</span>

::: {.question}
The line $ax+by=c$ has $a,b,c$ all non-zero. Which of the following is **necessary but not sufficient**

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $a$ and $b$ have the same sign &nbsp; **B** $b$ and $c$ have the same sign &nbsp;
**C** $a$ and $b$ have opposite signs &nbsp; **D** $b$ and $c$ have opposite signs &nbsp;
**E** $a$ and $c$ have opposite signs &nbsp; **F** $a$ and $c$ have the same sign

## Question 6 **[3]** &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">2021 · P2 Q15</span>

::: {.question}
A circle has equation $x^{2}+ax+y^{2}+by+c=0$, where $a,b,c$ are non-zero. Which is a **necessary and
sufficient** condition for the circle to be **tangent to the $y$-axis**?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $a^{2}=4c$ &nbsp; **B** $b^{2}=4c$ &nbsp;
**C** $\tfrac a2=\sqrt{\tfrac{a^{2}+b^{2}}{4}-c}$ &nbsp; **D** $\tfrac b2=\sqrt{\tfrac{a^{2}+b^{2}}{4}-c}$
&nbsp; **E** $-\tfrac a2=\sqrt{\tfrac{a^{2}+b^{2}}{4}-c}$ &nbsp;
**F** $-\tfrac b2=\sqrt{\tfrac{a^{2}+b^{2}}{4}-c}$
:::

## Question 7 **[3]** &nbsp;<span style="font-size:0.72em;color:#8a8a8a;font-weight:400">2023 · P2 Q13</span>

::: {.question}
Consider these five statements about a real number $x$. Which **one** of them is a **sufficient**
condition for **exactly three** of the other four?

&nbsp;&nbsp;**A** $x\ge0$
&nbsp;&nbsp;**B** $x=1$
&nbsp;&nbsp;**C** $x=0$ or $x=1$
&nbsp;&nbsp;**D** $x\ge0$ or $x\le1$
&nbsp;&nbsp;**E** $x\ge0$ and $x\le1$

*One of the five is true for every real number. Find it first.* **[3]**

Consider the equation
$$x^{3}-12x+k=0,$$
where $k$ is a real parameter.

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) Show that the equation has **exactly one** real root if and only if $\lvert k\rvert>16$. **[3]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;(b) For each condition below, say whether it is **sufficient**, **necessary**, **both**, or
**neither** for the equation to have exactly one real root. Justify each. **[3]**

&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;(i) $k>20$ &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; (ii) $k\neq0$ &nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp; (iii) $k^{2}>256$

&nbsp;&nbsp;(a) Give a condition on its **diagonals** that is **necessary and sufficient** for $ABCD$ to be

&nbsp;&nbsp;(c) "The diagonals are equal" is also necessary but not sufficient. Name a **different**

::: {.callout-tip}
## Before you hand this in

1. Every **"not sufficient"** and **"not necessary"** should have a concrete counterexample written next to
   it — a number, an equation, or a named shape. A verdict with no counterexample is an unsupported claim.
2. In Section C, check you wrote the **exact** condition down before looking at the options. Working
   straight from the options is what makes these questions feel like guesswork.
3. Re-read the **complete translation table** in the class material until you can place any phrase into its
   column without hesitating.
:::
